findings.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Deduction / Credit
findings.description: Indiana offers layered property tax relief for veterans through the Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs, currently structured as: (1) a 100% property tax deduction for veterans with a total disability who served at least 90 days, were honorably discharged, and have resided in Indiana at least one year before the assessment date; (2) a $350 credit for veterans who served during a war, were honorably discharged, and have a service-connected disability rating of 10% or more; (3) a $250 credit for veterans who served at least 90 days, were honorably discharged, are at least 62 years old, and have a disability rating of at least 10%; and (4) for homesteads conveyed to a veteran without consideration (e.g., by a nonprofit), a deduction matching the veteran's disability percentage (e.g., 50% disability yields a 50% assessed-value deduction, up to 100% for a totally disabled veteran). The officially posted page describes credits ($350/$250) rather than the older flat-dollar deduction amounts cited in some third-party summaries; this may reflect a 2026 legislative restructuring (referenced only in secondary sources, not independently confirmed against statute text this session), so figures here are taken directly from the current IDVA page rather than from any older or unconfirmed structure. No Indiana Code citation was visible on the fetched page, so legalCitation is left null rather than guessed.
findings.value: 100% deduction (total disability); $350 credit (10%+ disability, wartime service); $250 credit (age 62+ with 10%+ disability); percentage-matched deduction for gifted homesteads
otherReqs: Served at least 90 days (or during a period of war for the $350 credit)
Resided in Indiana at least 1 year before the assessment date
File with County Auditor using State Form 12662
findings.agency: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs / County Auditor
findings.sourceExcerpt: Served in the Armed Forces for at least 90 days; Received an honorable discharge; Have a total disability; and Resided in Indiana for at least one (1) year before the assessment date. ... $350 Credit: Served in the Armed Forces during a war; Received an honorable discharge; and Has a service-connected disability rating of 10% or more. ... $250 Credit: Served in the Armed Forces for at least 90 days; Received an honorable discharge; Is at least 62 years of age; and Has a disability rating of at least 10%.

findings.name: Indiana Veterans' Home (West Lafayette)
findings.description: The Indiana Veterans' Home in West Lafayette is the state's only veterans' home, offering long-term skilled nursing care, short-term rehabilitation, and memory care on a 250+ acre campus. It is open to honorably discharged veterans, their spouses or surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents (a parent of a service member who died while serving). Applicants must be Indiana residents for at least one year immediately preceding application, though residency waivers apply for those who enlisted from or were discharged to Indiana. There is no wartime-service requirement, and all applicants must pass a criminal background check. A claim seen in some secondary sources that 70%+ service-connected veterans receive free nursing care with no income limitation could not be confirmed on the official eligibility page fetched this session, so it is omitted here.
findings.value: Skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, and memory care for eligible veterans, spouses, and Gold Star parents
otherReqs: Honorable discharge (veteran); or spouse/surviving spouse of an honorably discharged veteran; or Gold Star parent
Indiana resident for at least 1 year before applying (waivers for those who enlisted from or discharged to Indiana)
Must pass a criminal background check
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service
findings.sourceExcerpt: An honorably discharged veteran of the United States armed forces, or the spouse (or surviving spouse) of an honorably discharged veteran ... A Gold Star parent, defined as a parent of a member of the U.S. military who died while serving in the Armed Forces ... There is no wartime service requirement in order to be eligible to apply for admission to the Indiana Veterans' Home. We accept all periods of service.

findings.name: Tuition and Fee Exemption for Children of Disabled or Deceased Veterans
findings.description: Indiana covers up to 100% of tuition and regularly assessed fees (up to 124 semester credit-hours) at Indiana public colleges and universities for the biological or legally-adopted children of veterans who served during a war (or hazardous duty recognized by a service/campaign medal) and who suffered a service-connected death or disability as determined by the VA. At private, non-profit Indiana colleges, the benefit is capped at up to $5,000 per year, but only for students graduating high school on or after January 1, 2023. For veterans who enlisted after 2011, a variable-coverage tier applies instead: 20% plus the veteran parent's VA disability percentage. The veteran parent must have an Indiana home of record on their DD-214 or have resided in Indiana at least 5 years before the student first applies. The student must apply before turning 33 and has 8 academic years to use the benefit.
findings.value: Up to 100% tuition/fees at Indiana public colleges (124 credit-hour cap); up to $5,000/year at private non-profit Indiana colleges (2023+ high school graduates); 20% + parent's VA disability percentage for post-2011 enlistees
otherReqs: Veteran parent served during a war or hazardous duty recognized by a service/campaign medal
Veteran parent had Indiana home of record on DD-214, or resided in Indiana 5+ years before student applies
Student is biological or adopted (before age 18) child of the veteran; stepchildren not eligible
Student applies before age 33; benefit usable for 8 academic years
Maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress; file FAFSA annually
findings.agency: Indiana Commission for Higher Education / Indiana Department of Veterans' Affairs
documentation: VA disability determination or service-connected death documentation
findings.sourceExcerpt: up to 100% of tuition and regularly assessed fees for up to 124 semester credit-hours ... up to $5,000 of tuition and regularly assessed fees ... Suffered a service connected death or disability as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs ... must first apply for this tuition and fee exemption before turning thirty-three (33) years old.

findings.name: State Merit System Veteran's Preference
findings.description: Indiana's State Merit System adds preference points for veterans applying for merit positions or promotions within Indiana state government, per Indiana Code 4-15-2-18. The official Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs employment-assistance page confirms the existence of this preference-point program but does not itself state the exact number of points or the percentage added to exam scores; secondary (non-.gov) sources describe a 10%-of-total-score addition with an honorable discharge and 181+ days of active duty as the eligibility bar, but that specific figure could not be confirmed against a directly-read official source this session, so it is flagged as unconfirmed rather than stated as fact.
findings.value: Preference points added to civil service examination/promotion scores for eligible veterans (exact point value not confirmed via a directly-read official source this session)
otherReqs: Honorable discharge (exact minimum service length not confirmed via a directly-read official source this session)
findings.sourceExcerpt: The State Merit System provides for the addition of points for veterans applying for merit positions or promotions within State Government.

findings.name: Disabled Hoosier Veteran License Plate
findings.description: Indiana issues a Disabled Hoosier Veteran license plate carrying handicapped parking privileges to veterans with a service-connected disability resulting in: loss of sight or permanent vision impairment in both eyes; loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet; loss or permanent loss of use of one or both hands; a physical condition precluding the applicant from walking without pain or difficulty; or a disability rating of at least 50% with at least 60% of that rating attributed to mobility issues. Applicants submit the VA award letter (with the breakdown of individual disability ratings) and a DD-214 to the Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs. Vehicles registered with this plate are not exempt from registration fees or property taxes on the vehicle.
findings.value: Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate with handicapped parking privileges; no separate registration fee or tax exemption attached to the plate itself
otherReqs: Service-connected disability meeting one of the specified mobility/vision/limb criteria, or 50%+ rating with 60%+ attributed to mobility
Unauthorized use by a non-owner is a Class C infraction and can result in plate revocation
documentation: USDVA Award Letter with breakdown of individual disability ratings
DD Form 214 or other proof of military discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: A "disabled veteran" must have a service-connected disability resulting in one of five conditions: (1) loss of sight or permanent vision impairment in both eyes; (2) loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet; (3) loss or permanent loss of use of one or both hands; (4) a physical condition that precludes the applicant from being able to walk without pain or difficulty; or (5) at least 50% disability rating with at least 60% attributed to mobility issues.

findings.name: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) Hunting & Fishing License
findings.description: Indiana residents who are veterans with a documented service-connected disability qualify for a discounted DAV license covering small-game hunting and fishing (excluding stamps) for $2.75 per year, or $27.50 for a 10-year license. The DAV license does not cover deer, turkey, waterfowl, or trout/salmon stamps, which must be purchased separately at regular price. Separately, catastrophically disabled Indiana veterans may hunt without any license or state stamp on a small number of specially designated days each year (four days were designated in 2025).
findings.value: Discounted small-game hunting and fishing license: $2.75/year or $27.50 for a 10-year license; free stamp-less hunting for catastrophically disabled veterans on designated days
otherReqs: Application certified by a County Veteran Service Officer or the Indiana Department of Veterans' Affairs
documentation: Certification from Indiana Department of Veterans' Affairs
findings.sourceExcerpt: Indiana residents who have served in the armed forces and have a documented service-connected disability are eligible. ... covers the hunting of small game as well as fishing, excluding any stamps.

findings.name: State Income Tax Deduction for Military Retirement and Survivor's Benefits Pay
findings.description: For 2022 and later tax years, Indiana allows a deduction equal to the entire amount of military retirement income and/or survivor's benefits received, effectively exempting that income from state income tax. This is a full-population phase-in that reached 100% in 2022 after ramping from 25% (2019) to 50% (2020) to 75% (2021), per Indiana Department of Revenue guidance. This is separate from VA disability compensation and pension payments, which are excluded from taxable income under federal law and were not separately itemized as an Indiana-specific benefit in the source consulted this session.
findings.value: 100% state income tax deduction for military retirement and survivor's benefits pay (2022 and later tax years)
otherReqs: Reporting military retirement income and/or survivor's benefits on an Indiana state income tax return
documentation: 1099-R or other documentation of military retirement/survivor's benefits income
findings.sourceExcerpt: For 2022 and later, the deduction is equal to the entire amount of military retirement income and/or survivor's benefits.
